item.title: Scientists fooled 11 bat species with fake water covered in clear plastic
item.description: Bats often confuse smooth artificial surfaces for water through their echolocation abilities. Researchers discovered that multiple bat species, including those still inexperienced with water, persistently tried to drink from these misleading surfaces. This intriguing behavior underscores the significant role of echolocation in shaping bats' environmental perceptions and suggests that artificial surfaces can emit deceptive acoustic cues that alter their natural behaviour.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Worms turn human waste into compost, but parasitic eggs can survive the process
item.description: Research indicates that tiger worms did not decompose Ascaris eggs present in faecal waste during lab trials. The eggs remained intact and capable of survival following prolonged exposure to the worms. A majority of the eggs were discovered within the coir layer of the biodigesters. As a result, the produced vermicompost and effluent must not be deemed safe for farming, necessitating additional testing for products from tiger worm toilets.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Watch: Deadly pyrotechnic explosion rocks church festival in Mexico, 10 killed
item.description: During a vibrant religious festival, a tragic pyrotechnic explosion claimed the lives of at least ten individuals and left sixty-four injured. The catastrophe took place near the Nuestra Señora de la Luz church in Temascalcingo, where walls crumbled amidst chaos as fireworks malfunctioned. The explosion was linked to a traditional ritual featuring a straw bull equipped with fireworks, and officials are currently investigating the cause of this heartbreaking event.
item.dc:creator: Vijaya Srivastava

item.title: Pat McAfee has put more than $6 million of his own money into GameDay prizes and charity
item.description: An LSU student named Bruce had a chance at a million-dollar reward during a broadcast sponsored by Pat McAfee and Home Depot. Selected randomly from the crowd, he attempted a 33-yard field goal twice but unfortunately missed both shots. This challenge comes on the heels of prior seasons where students successfully claimed large cash prizes along with donations to charity.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Pennsylvania couple preserves 78.3 acres, helping eliminate plans for 88 homes and 21 condos
item.description: A Pennsylvania couple, Paul and Cynthia Black, bought 78.3 acres in 2022 with preservation in mind. The property is now permanently protected through a conservation easement, expanding a 236-acre corridor. Their broader conservation efforts across three contiguous projects have eliminated plans for 88 houses and 21 condominiums, preserving farmland, woodland and clean water.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: In 2014, a tech entrepreneur bought a 1,100-acre Sonoma ranch for $12 million and spent...
item.description: A remarkable 1,100-acre estate on Sonoma Mountain has been sold for an astounding $38.5 million. Entrepreneurs Mark and Debra Leslie have converted this once undeveloped land into a self-sustaining retreat, pouring in $33 million for environmental restoration and diverse farming infrastructures. The property boasts a contemporary main residence with breathtaking views, showcasing the growing interest in secluded, off-grid homes in coastal California.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Joy Behar sells $4.75 million Hamptons home for $5.65 million after listing it for $10.95 million
item.description: The View host Joy Behar has sold her historic 1903 Hamptons home in Sag Harbor for $5.65 million, after initially listing it for $10.95 million. TheViewhost bought the four-bedroom property for $4.75 million in 2016. The sale followed multiple price cuts and an unusual strategy that saw the asking price later increase.
item.dc:creator: TOI Real Estate Desk

item.title: In 1997, Texas mixed discarded roofing shingles into two 1,000-foot Highway 31 test sections
item.description: Engineers in Texas have made groundbreaking progress by recycling discarded roofing shingles into robust road surfaces. After extensive testing, these innovative materials showed they could match the performance of conventional asphalt, enduring significant traffic wear. The success of this pilot program also spurred the implementation of state-wide regulations that promote the use of recycled shingles in highway construction, leading to both cost savings and conservation of natural resources.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A company bought 7,500 acres of England for £8.5 million to create ‘Britain’s Yellowstone'
item.description: A pioneering nature restoration firm has acquired Emblehope Moor to embark on a significant rewilding initiative. This visionary endeavor seeks to establish a thriving wildlife haven in northern England, while ensuring investors receive returns on their contributions prior to the land transfer. The project focuses on revitalizing peatlands and eliminating invasive tree species, all while valuing and utilizing local expertise for effective rewilding practices.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: After Brecksville Dam was removed, free-flowing habitat linked to Lake Erie more than doubled to 71 km
item.description: A restored Lake Erie wetland saw millions of aquatic animals after reconnection to waterways. High-resolution sonar tracked over 3.4 million fish movements into and out of the marsh. Fish utilized the habitat throughout the day and night, showing continuous usage patterns. This research provides clear evidence of how aquatic species use restored coastal habitats. The findings inform management decisions for Great Lakes coastal wetland restoration efforts.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Lululemon founder Chip Wilson divorcing wife Shannon ‘Summer’ Wilson; no prenup, $1.1B stakes
item.description: Chip Wilson, founder of Lululemon, has filed for divorce from wife Shannon ‘Summer’ Wilson after 20 years of marriage. The couple reportedly had no prenuptial agreement. Wilson owns an 8.6% stake in Lululemon worth nearly $1 billion, while Shannon holds about 1%, valued at $100 million, leaving their substantial assets in focus.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Fuentes Criticises Owens Focus: Far-right pundit says she hijacked Kirk tributes; urges return to faith
item.description: Nick Fuentes has criticized Candace Owens over her coverage of Charlie Kirk’s death, arguing that the conversation has shifted away from Kirk’s influence on young men. Fuentes said Kirk inspired followers through his faith, work ethic, family values and public message. He also condemned what he described as excessive speculation and personal investigations, urging people to resist cynicism and focus instead on conscience, goodness and the values they believe Kirk represented.
